The main takeaway from our work is that

the atomic-mix fraction in the hot spot is not a simple function of the capsule fill time, but rather a complex function that depends on many other parameters, including the hohlraum size and the ablator material.

the measured atomic-mix values are in agreement with simulations that include the effect of the ablator gas in the hohlraum, which indicates that the atomic mix in these experiments is dominated by the ablator-gas interaction in the hohl-raum and not by the interaction between the ablator and the hot-spot gas.
the atomic ablator mix into the hot spot is significantly less than predicted by simulations, which is consistent with the results from the first NIF ignition campaign.
